title: Name, speech, mind, will, thought — the ladder (7.1–7.5)
hook: Narada keeps asking one question, sir, is there anything greater than this? and every time, the answer is yes

segments.voice: Yesterday: Narada comes to Sanatkumara, the learned sage who says I know only words, not the self. Your line was knowledge isn't it. Did you notice a feeling instead of reaching for a fact? Day three hundred fifty-three.
screen: `NARADA COMES TO SANATKUMARA — KNOWLEDGE ISN'T IT.`

segments.voice: Kids discover a game early. Why? Because. But why? Because of this. But why that? It drives parents up the wall. And yet it's how you get to the bottom of things: you just keep asking for the next layer down. Sanatkumara has told Narada that everything he studied is only name. And Narada, to his credit, doesn't argue. He asks the next question. Sir, is there anything greater than name? And so begins the ladder.
screen: `WHY? BECAUSE. BUT WHY?` → `ALL YOU KNOW IS ONLY NAME.` → `IS THERE ANYTHING GREATER?`

segments.voice: The first rung is name. Sanatkumara says: revere name as Brahman. As far as name reaches, you'll have freedom there. A fair start. Names are how we hold the world. Is there anything greater than name? Yes, speech is greater. Speech makes the Vedas known, and earth and sky, and right and wrong, true and false. If there were no speech, Sanatkumara says, right and wrong couldn't be made known at all. Is there anything greater than speech? Yes, mind. And here comes a lovely image: as a closed fist holds two small fruits, mind holds both speech and name. When you think in your mind, let me learn these verses, then you learn them. Let me do this, then you do it. Greater than mind? Will, the Sanskrit samkalpa, intention. When you intend something, then you think it, then you say it, then you give it a name. Greater than will? Thought, citta, attention, the awareness that notices what's going on before you even intend. And Sanatkumara says something pointed here. If someone knows a great deal but has no real attention, people say: he's nobody. If someone knows little but is truly attentive, people want to listen. Look at the direction of the climb. Name, speech, mind, will, thought. Each rung is quieter and more inward than the last, and each one holds the one below it. Narada came in with a mountain of names. Sanatkumara is walking him up and in, toward the one who's paying attention. And at every rung, Narada asks again: is there anything greater?
screen: `NAME: HOW WE HOLD THE WORLD.` · `SPEECH: RIGHT AND WRONG MADE KNOWN.` · `MIND HOLDS BOTH, LIKE A FIST.` · `WILL, THEN THOUGHT.` · then, large: `EACH IS GREATER.`

segments.voice: Today's practice climbs the ladder inward. Sit and settle. Notice a name in your mind: anyone's, anything's. Then notice the inner voice that says it: speech. Then the mind behind the voice, where thoughts form. Then the intention under the thought, the pull toward something. Then the plain attention that notices all of it. Rest at that top rung, just noticing, for as long as you can. When you slip down, climb again. The bell holds the time.
Name. The first rung of Sanatkumara's ladder; above it, speech, mind, will and thought, each greater than the last.
Your line: each is greater. Today, before you say something important, notice the intention under it, the rung below the words. Day three hundred fifty-three.

howItsDone: Teachers of Vedanta often walk students up Sanatkumara's ladder as a contemplative exercise, moving attention from words to mind to awareness.

pairs: holds speech and name, like a fist

myth: he says revere name as Brahman; as far as name reaches, there's freedom. then there's something greater.
mind holds speech and name like a fist holds two small fruits
a person who knows little but is truly attentive is listened to
Sanatkumara says so of citta, thought.

fork.setup: you're Narada. Sanatkumara has just told you that everything you studied is only name. what do you do?
options: argue that your learning is more than names.
ask: sir, is there anything greater than name?
fork.reveal: he asks, and keeps asking at every rung. each time the answer is yes: speech, mind, will, thought, and more to come.

original.note: Sanskrit nāma: name. the first rung of Sanatkumara's ladder.

trapdoor: what you thought: a list of mental faculties.
what it means: a ladder inward. each rung holds the one below: name, speech, mind, will, thought.
what a scholar hears: Chandogya 7.1–7.5. each step uses the same formula: revere it as Brahman; as far as it reaches, freedom; is there anything greater? the ladder runs on to prana in 7.15.

notes: The fist image (7.3.1): two amalaka or kola fruits, or two aksha nuts; rendered 'two small fruits'. Confirm.
citta rendered 'thought, attention'; translators vary (thought, intelligence, consciousness). Confirm.
Trapdoor says the ladder runs on to prana (7.15) before bhuman (7.23); confirm.
